evidence_set: Unspecified deaths were reallocated in each state and year in proportion to the opioid share of deaths with a named drug, an assumption the authors call rather strong: this added more than 70,000 potential opioid-related deaths for 1999–2015 and 5,662 in 2015 (editors' sum of the Table 2 column; the text says more than 5,600), beside 29,383 reported; Pennsylvania's 2015 rate rose from 9.90 to 20.12 per 100,000 (+103%), while rates changed by less than 1% in Connecticut, Washington DC, New Hampshire, Maine and Rhode Island. No unspecified death was checked against toxicology or case records.
